title: ARM LAB: JOINTS, TORQUE, AND CONTACT
subtitle: Drive to the calibration gate, then inspect a four-joint arm whose pose comes from the physical plant.
briefing: MISSION: reach the calibration gate with zero collisions and settle the chassis.
INSPECT: the four arm links are separate MuJoCo bodies; each mesh is bound to its live joint frame.
PROVE: joint axes, effort, encoder feedback, COM, and contact are engineering evidence, not shortcuts into ROBOT.

shots.title: THE BASE OWNS THE ARM ROOT
shots.caption: The arm base is mounted from the robot profile. Its first joint origin and axis are part of the same physical model as the drive wheels.

shots.title: EACH LINK HAS A REAL JOINT
shots.caption: The upper arm follows its MuJoCo body and joint pose. The viewer never integrates a decorative angle from wall-clock time.

shots.title: THE TOOL RESPONDS TO EFFORT
shots.caption: Operator effort is bounded, expires through the same watchdog, and is checked against encoder freshness before reaching the plant.

shots.title: ARRIVAL IS TWO INDEPENDENT VERDICTS
shots.caption: ROBOT decides from measurements and estimates. SIM separately checks physical clearance, contact, and the settled stop.

walkaround.title: SHOULDER JOINT / AXIS
walkaround.lesson: The first link starts at the configured arm base. Its axis and pose are read directly from MuJoCo.

walkaround.title: ELBOW JOINT / LOAD
walkaround.lesson: Joint damping and torque limits are plant parameters. A visual link cannot move without the simulated joint responding.

walkaround.title: TOOL / ENCODER FEEDBACK
walkaround.lesson: The tool is the fourth joint link. Real hardware uses the same typed arm encoder and effort contract.

walkaround.title: COM AND CONTACT
walkaround.lesson: Engineering view can show center of mass, collision geometry, joint axes, and live contact normals. These remain SIM evidence.

prediction.question: What should happen when arm effort is removed while the arm is moving?

choices.label: The links coast and settle under damping and gravity
choices.explanation: The plant applies the configured torque limits, damping, gravity, and contacts. The renderer only reads the resulting joint poses.

choices.label: The viewer snaps each link to a target angle
choices.explanation: A draw-time animation would violate the MuJoCo pose contract and is not an accepted result.

choices.label: The arm lesson has no physical evidence
choices.explanation: A run without a terminal mission or usable feedback is incomplete evidence.

running_prompt: Use Engineering view to inspect joint axes, COM, contacts, and encoder feedback. In sandbox mode H enables chassis/arm operator input: I/K, O/L, P/;, [/'].

lessons: A manipulator is an articulated physical system: link geometry, joint axis, torque, damping, COM, and contact all matter.
The renderer consumes MuJoCo body and joint read-back; it does not invent a second arm state.
ROBOT receives encoder measurements and accepted commands, never simulator contact truth or score.
